title: How to write spokesperson quotes journalists actually use
hook: "We are thrilled to announce…" is the most deleted sentence in PR. 😅

sources.name: Cision
sources.title: 2025 State of the Media Report (press release, 7 May 2025)

slides.title: the "thrilled" test
slides.body: If the quote would fit any company's release, it fits none. Delete "thrilled", "proud", "excited" and see what's left.
slides.ex:
✕ "We are thrilled to launch our new app."
✓ "Half our orders come after 9PM. The app is built for people who shop after their shift."

slides.title: give an *opinion*, not a summary
slides.body: The body of the release covers the facts. The quote is where a human explains **why it matters** or **what happens next**.

slides.title: one number, *said like a person*
slides.body: Numbers make quotes quotable, but read them out loud first. If it sounds like a spreadsheet, rewrite it.
slides.ex:
✕ "Revenue increased by 37.42% YoY."
✓ "We grew by more than a third this year, mostly outside Metro Manila."

slides.title: keep it *under 40 words*
slides.body: Reporters trim long quotes or skip them. Two sentences: the point, then the reason.

slides.label: of journalists call press releases the *most useful* PR resource
slides.body: A quote that can be lifted word for word is part of what makes a release usable.

slides.title: quote checklist
items: States a view or what happens next
At most one number, said naturally

slides.title: write it like they'll *quote it*
items: Send it to whoever drafts your CEO quotes

lines: 02 Give an opinion, not a summary
03 One number, said like a person
captions_meta.li_hook:
The quote is the only part of a press release where a person speaks. Most companies waste it.
How to write one a journalist will actually use.
li_body: Cision's 2025 State of the Media found 72% of journalists call press releases the most useful resource from PR teams. What makes a release usable is that parts of it can be lifted as is, and the quote is the most common candidate.
li_points: The "thrilled" test: if the quote fits any company's release, rewrite it.
Opinion over summary: explain why it matters or what happens next.
One number, phrased the way a person would say it.
Under 40 words, two sentences: the point, then the reason.
captions_meta.li_close: What's the worst quote you've been asked to approve? (No names, please.)
captions_meta.fb: Quotes that journalists actually use, with before & after examples. Save this before your next release 👇
